listing.name: Final Fantasy Fables: Chocobo’s Dungeon (darkuni Recomp)
listing.summary: Play Chocobo's Dungeon with darkuni's Windows recompilation and your own NTSC-U Wii disc image.

steps.title: Prepare your disc image
steps.instruction: Copy your own NTSC-U Chocobo's Dungeon disc image (R7FEGD, .iso or .ciso) beside chocobo.exe, and keep your original separately. On first start the game extracts it into its extracted folder, which takes up to a minute; after that the copied image is no longer needed. You can instead put the sys and files folders of an already extracted disc into extracted.

steps.title: Build the windowed Linux player from your original
steps.instruction: Follow the tagged upstream build instructions. Obtain sys/main.dol from your own matching extracted disc and run the documented Python recompilation into a clean gen directory. Build the windowed USE_SDL=ON target with CMake, Ninja, a C++17 compiler, SDL2 and OpenGL development libraries.

steps.title: Keep each profile with its actual root
steps.instruction: Use the upstream player with the matching extracted sys and files. With the standard layout preserve extracted, nand and chocobo.ini beside the creating runtime. The Windows player also accepts an explicit extracted-folder path, where save placement can follow that external root. Preserve the actual data locations before switching layouts.

warnings: The package includes recompiled game code that the project license does not cover. Portcove downloads it only from the project’s own releases. You need your own original game files.
Keep the upstream folder outside the Portcove library. Close the game before backing up or replacing the creating runtime and its data.
The Linux instructions cover the windowed source route. The upstream headless EGL test build is a separate target.

presentation.manual_preparation: Before first Play, copy your own NTSC-U Chocobo's Dungeon disc image (R7FEGD, .iso or .ciso) into the managed folder beside chocobo.exe, and keep your original separately. On first Play the game extracts it into its extracted folder, which takes up to a minute; without an image it shows Game files not found and closes. Once the game has started, delete the copied image so it is not kept in backups. If the first start was interrupted or used the wrong image, delete the extracted folder and start again with the right image in place. The download is the recompiled program with SDL2 and contains no game data; the project license does not cover the recompiled game code. Portcove preserves extracted, nand (saves) and chocobo.ini across updates and backups. A start path you give chocobo.exe yourself is outside Portcove and keeps saves beside that folder. The game needs a GPU with OpenGL 3.3. Portcove replaces the program; upstream owns disc import and save formats.
